objective: Measure S3's rebalance timing luck across 21 signal-day offsets and test whether a four-tranche version lowers drawdown without giving up Sharpe or the G1 bar. The result only feeds the S3 rule renewal after 2026-11-01 and the execution plan of a future live pilot; the live rule is frozen.
target_regime_and_horizon: Same regime S3 is valid for: US leveraged equity/sector ETF momentum. Stress 2016-05-02..2023-08-31, select 2023-09-18..2025-12-31, anchor 2024-01-08..2026-09-16 (frozen gate), 2026-01-02..2026-09-17 contaminated, reported only.
existing_solution_comparison: Tranching is an established published remedy (Hoffstein et al. 2019/2020; Concretum 2025; Allocate Smartly offers it for live models). Nothing to invent; the only missing piece is S3-specific: its own offset dispersion and whether four tranches change its drawdown under the vt40 and dip-boost overlay. `oc research directions check tranch` found no prior local test.
remaining_evidence_gap: Published work reports mean and dispersion, not drawdown, and none covers a two-ETF leveraged rotation with a volatility target.
negative_experiments_checked: H-20260927-01 (sleeve combination, 0/3): lower drawdown came only from lower exposure; this round keeps exposure identical, so any drawdown change is timing, not deleveraging. dir:levered_single_asset_sma_trend_gate (refuted by calendar-shift placebo): reminds that a single date choice can dominate a levered backtest, which is why the 21-offset distribution is reported in full.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Frozen engine: signal at close, fill next open, 10 bp per side primary, 20 bp stress, cost on netted account turnover. T4 averages the four tranches' effective weights, so offsetting trades net inside one account. Live execution would need four order dates a month; min-trade tolerance in the live runner is not modelled.
stop_condition: If T4 fails any of the four preregistered conditions, keep month-end single-date execution for S3 and do not propose tranching at renewal.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: One run of the frozen S3 engine at 21 signal offsets plus T4 (22 candidates, daily ETF panel, under a minute of compute).
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: T4 vs O00: shallower net-10bp max drawdown in both anchor and stress; Sharpe not lower by more than 0.05 in either; anchor G1 or G1' at 10 and 20 bp.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: Any of the four conditions false.

sources.claim: In a concentrated (20-stock) monthly-rebalanced US momentum portfolio, 1991-2024, the CAGR gap between the best and worst trading day of the month was 348 bp; splitting into 2-20 tranches left the mean CAGR (16.7-16.8%) and Sharpe (0.59-0.60) unchanged while shrinking the dispersion from 3.48% to 0-2%. Single-day max drawdowns ranged -69.3% to -74.9%.
sources.applicability: Prior for T4 vs O00; see external-brief.json.
sources.limitations: Snapshot is pdftotext of the fetched PDF (PDF kept beside it). Stock-level momentum, no costs in the RTL table, not leveraged ETFs, no drawdown figures for the tranched books.
sources.independent_replication: Hoffstein, Faber, Braun (SSRN 3673910) report >100 bp annualized RTL for momentum and other factor indices.

sources.claim: Factor indices (value, size, momentum, quality, low vol) show rebalance timing luck often above 100 bp annualized, larger for concentrated and less frequently rebalanced portfolios.
